items.title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle detained for allegedly cutting off ankle monitor, officials say
items.description: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.

items.title: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
items.description: Najib Razak was convicted for his role in the billion-dollar scandal involving the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund.

items.title: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
items.description: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.

items.title: Violence erupts in Bangladesh as ousted PM's supporters stage protest
items.description: Supporters of Sheikh Hasina want her to return from exile in India.

items.title: Spain's king and queen attend memorial service for rail crash victims
items.description: Sixty-nine people died in the collision near Toledo two weeks ago and 28 are still in hospital.

items.title: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
items.description: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.

items.title: Board of Peace says Israel's aid response after Gaza floods 'insufficent'
items.description: The group, formed by Trump, issues rare criticism of Israel, while also blaming Hamas for the suffering of civilians in Gaza.

items.title: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
items.description: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.

items.title: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
items.description: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.

items.title: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
items.description: With 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and joined the fight against the occupying German forces.

items.title: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
items.description: The US Food and Drug Administration says Ozempic, Wegovy, and other weight-loss drugs must have labels about the condition, known as NAION.

items.title: Arrests made after visit from former US President Biden
items.description: Joe Biden was in Dublin to see his son Hunter awarded the Gold Medal for Outstanding Contribution for Public Discourse

items.title: Twelve dead after motorway pile-ups in Bulgaria fog
items.description: About 50 other people were injured in the pile-ups along a section of the Trakia motorway, officials have said.

items.title: US federal authorities could have prevented Epstein crimes, report finds
items.description: The report by a Republican-led congressional committee follows a 15-month investigation into the handling of the late disgraced financier's case.

items.title: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
items.description: The Ritz hotel in Paris, which is still owned by the Al Fayed family, is one of the properties searched by police.

items.title: Police officer dies and another injured after backpack explosion in northern Spain
items.description: Officers attended the scene in connection with a separate incident at a residential building in the Spanish city.

items.title: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being 'cowards'
items.description: The Congolese army's fight against rebel groups has long been hampered by disarray within its ranks.

items.title: 'Cruise for life' ship seized in Singapore
items.description: The Odyssey was meant to take guests around the world for years, but the trip was cut short after its operator ran out of money.

items.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.description: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.

items.title: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
items.description: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
